title: Fugaro accounts pool ls
description: The document `fugaro accounts pool ls --json` prints: the project, its pools, and each pool's members with the state that holds them and the figures the service counts (docs/model-credentials-routing/contract-pools.md, F19). The document is the listing's own shape and not a reference: `rule` is the pool's own, as its owner wrote it, and is empty where the pool names none -- the listing resolves nothing, so a reader that needs the resolved rule reads it through the pool's `strategy` (R21, routing.Rule.RuleOrDefault). The figures arrive with PL10 and are ABSENT until then, which is why `next_reset`, `usage` and `headroom` are nullable and why a member nothing holds is `available`: a figure the service has not counted is never guessed. It is display data and never an input to an authorization decision, and it carries names and figures and never a value (F19): no token, no key and no secret appears here, for anyone. No object is closed for the reason the other listing documents state: a consumer that refused a member this schema does not know would refuse a newer CLI's document, and the closed shape is the Go type the command marshals (routing.PoolListDoc).

project.description: The project whose pools these are, as the selected config names it. Empty when no project config was selected, which leaves the pool list empty too.

pools.description: The project's pools, in the order the config lists them. An empty list is a fact -- the project has no pool -- and never a null (routing.PoolListDoc.MarshalJSON).

pool.description: One pool and who it belongs to.

rule.$comment: routing.Rule: the three of the contract's rule column, and "" for a pool whose owner wrote none -- the member carries no omitempty, so a pool that names no rule prints an empty string rather than leaving the key out.
rule.description: How the service picks among the pool's members, as the pool's owner wrote it. Empty where the pool names none.

principal.description: Whose pool it is (D3181): an identity and never display text, and not a reading of `owner`, which stays an email address.

threshold.$comment: routing.Threshold.Valid: greater than 0 and at most 1 (D3178, PL1's validation and PL8's picker read the same bound).
threshold.description: The pool's optional usage threshold: the fraction of a member's limit at which the pool moves off that member. Null where the pool names none.

members.description: The pool's members, in the order its owner listed them, which is the order `ordered` walks and the order a round robin turns in.

principal.$comment: routing.Principal, whose kind and id both carry no omitempty: a pool that names no principal prints {"kind":"","id":""} and never an absent member.

kind.description: What the pool's principal is (D3181). Empty where the pool names no principal.

id.description: The principal's own identifier: a person's Google subject, a service account's address, or the project's name. A name and never a value.

member.description: One member of a pool: what holds it, what it has spent, and what is left of it.

name.description: The member's name -- a container's, in the project's or the principal's own namespace -- and never its value (F19).

state.$comment: creds.State's words, which `fugaro accounts ls --json` already prints; "available" is a member nothing holds (creds.StateAvailable), and it is what this command prints for every member until PL10 fills the figures.
state.description: What holds the member, in internal/creds' own words.

next_reset.description: When the member becomes usable again -- a mark's own instant, or the time its leases lapse -- and null when nothing holds it.

usage.description: What the member has spent in the window the service counts (PL10), and null where the service counts nothing for it.

headroom.description: The fraction of the member's limit that is left, where the provider reported a utilisation figure, and null otherwise: it is never guessed (D3178, U1).

usage.description: What one member has spent in the current window (PL10).

calls.description: How many calls the member has served in the window.

tokens.description: How many tokens those calls spent. A count and not a price.
